purpose: STEP 3 of the owner-approved improvement sequence: zero-shot scoring of the SERVING Arm-1 export (b5-universal-arm1-2026-005, export/model.pt sha c6604a68; 7 languages, no Cameroonian language) on the 11 Cameroonian languages that no MedZen model has been adapted on (fub, dua, bbj, bkm, fmp, bax, nmg, bkh, mua, eto, wes), over the pinned two-field decode manifest sha 66c757f0 (no reference text leaves the engineering host). Normalized input convention, greedy CTC, plain decode (no probability dump). PREREGISTERED DESCRIPTIVE READING (no gate, nothing promotable): tone-sensitive CER (asr-eval-norm-v3-tone-sensitive, pooled over characters) is primary, WER secondary, reported per language and surface: cv_test (the frozen speaker+prompt-disjoint holdout, 3-6 speakers), cv_all (test + dev + <=20 train clips per train speaker, 199 of 204 speakers) and soreva (single male speaker; for eto, nmg and bkh SOREVA uses a different spelling system, so CV and SOREVA are not comparable there). Speaker-clustered 95% intervals only where a surface has >= 5 speakers. Paired model differences on identical clips: arm1-minus-base and icmp15-minus-base. Stated hypotheses, descriptive only: H1 Arm-1 (trained on Nigerian Pidgin) reads Cameroonian Pidgin (wes) better than base; H2 the 15-language pilot helps close relatives of its trained languages (bbj, fmp: East Bamileke with byv; bax: Mbam-Nkam with byv/nnh/nla; eto: A70 with ewo; bkh: A40 with bas) more than unrelated ones (fub, mua). Labels per language on cv_all CER for the best model: < 10 near-usable zero-shot, 10-25 adaptation candidate, > 25 needs data - labels, not decisions. 'Unseen' means not in any MedZen adaptation run; pretraining exposure of the base model is unknown (Meta lists training hours for some of these codes). One attempt per job, no retry, no follow-on run, no serving change; Arm-1 keeps serving.
scope: EXPLORATORY DIAGNOSTIC SCORING ONLY. No promotion, registry write, serving change or deployment. Arm-1 keeps serving.
worst_case_basis: 3,600 s ceiling on ml.g6.xlarge at $1.60/h on-demand = $1.60. 14,652 rows / 19.67 h of audio; the 18,759-row bmpair-base decode on this evaluator family billed 2,301 s, and the fitted rate (~0.12 s per row + ~100 s fixed) predicts about 1,300-1,900 s. The ceiling is the cap, not an estimate.
